chunks: And in the narration of Muḥammad ibn Ḥumrān, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, he said:

If a woman says to her husband, in a statement, ‘I will not obey any command of yours,’ whether explained in detail or not explained, then what he has taken from her becomes permissible for him, and he has no return to her.

key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the wife/woman involved in the ruling
key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: the husband’s right to revoke the divorce and return her
key_terms.لَا أُطِيعُ: I will not obey, expressing refusal of marital continuation
key_terms.لِزَوْجِهَا: to her husband, indicating the marital legal context

ai.seo_question: When does a khulʿ divorce become final so that the husband has no right to take his wife back?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning khulʿ, where the wife expresses decisive unwillingness to remain under the husband’s authority. In such a case, the compensation taken from her is lawful for him, and he does not retain the right of الرجعة (revocation/return) over her.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4823 - In the narration of Muhammad ibn Humran from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), that Imam (as) said:

"If a woman says to her husband, in any form, 'I will not obey any of your commands,' whether she explains it in detail or not, it becomes permissible for him to take what he has taken from her, and he has no right to take her back."
